title: The 1963 Japan tour
summary: Asked to go to Japan, he tours three months with Lewis's group, is in Tokyo the day the president is assassinated, and returns in December 1963.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah. And George, yeah. That's right. Yeah, that was the All-Stars that played then. And, uh... Well, first thing, next thing came up was Japan. Yes. Jeff asked him, said, Joe, you'd like to go to Japan? I said, yeah, what is Spain? He told me.

That was 1963, up in office, I believe. I told him, yeah. I said, who with? He said, well, Joe Band, George. I said, well, all right. Well, Jim didn't want to go. So you got Nelson, George, Papa John Joseph, Robichaud piano, I was on drums, and Punch. And we all agreed to go. He said, there was a three-month tour. I said, yeah, I don't mind it. Well, we went over there, and we really made a smashing hit with the people. They really went for jazz, like hook, line, and sinker. They loved it. And we stayed over there for them three months. And we went back to Tokyo. Well, we came back to Tokyo the day that the president was assassinated. I think we were stopping at the Prince Hotel. And they had the news in the paper, you know, over there in American, you know, so you could read it. Well, they claimed two holidays for the whole of Japan, which I thought was very nice of them, very respectable of them. And we left the following day, and we went back to Honolulu. We didn't play. We stayed there for a couple of days. And we left by plane and came back to New Orleans on the 3rd of December 1963. And I've been home ever since.
That was the last tour you went on?
That was the last tour I went on. So...
You didn't go on any other trips to Japan? No.
